groups.claim: RiskPatternSpecification: A managed, reusable information specification of risk-relevant conditions and possible effects. Its identity is distinct from a particular risk case, a scenario execution and the uncertain effects themselves.
RiskContextSpecification: A versioned information specification of analysis boundaries, circumstances, time horizon and objective references under which risk statements and results are interpreted.

RiskScenarioSpecification: A managed information specification of a possible development of conditions, events and effects concerning one or more RiskCases. Several scenarios may concern one case; a scenario is not the case or an actual occurrence.
RiskOccurrence: An actual occurrence or change relevant to a risk scenario; a scenario or report alone does not establish that it happened.
RiskNatureAssertion: A source-qualified information assertion that possible or reported effects are favorable, unfavorable or mixed relative to identified objectives and context.

NatureTerm: A controlled value used to qualify the nature of effects relative to objectives; it does not classify risk independently of context. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.

RiskSource: A contextual source role that an entity may play in giving rise to risk, alone or with other contributors. The catalog boundary spans possible bearer categories and is not assigned a single OntoUML stereotype here.

PredisposingCondition: A risk-relevant situation that increases susceptibility to specified occurrences or effects. Reference to it requires explicit source support and does not establish a causal mechanism.

Trigger: An actual occurrence interpreted as initiating a risk-relevant development in a specified context. A hypothetical trigger description is represented as scenario content, not as an actual Trigger individual.

Consequence: An outcome relevant to objectives, considered as a referent distinct from a statement about it. Outcomes can have different ontological categories; no universal event or object stereotype is asserted.

Vulnerability: An intrinsic susceptibility of a bearer to specified risk-relevant conditions or effects. The proposed mode interpretation requires a supported bearer; security-specific exploitation meanings remain source-qualified.
Exposure: A time-qualified situation relating an affected bearer to a risk source or relevant condition. An exposure score or its description is information about that situation.
RiskState: A temporally qualified state of a risk-relevant situation, distinct from the workflow status of its record.

InformationArtifact: A managed documentary object with an instituted identity that persists across its descriptions and issued versions. Artifact identity is distinct from a file path, a storage row and semantic content.

ArtifactVersion: An identifiable issued documentary version of a managed information artifact. Its issued semantic content and effective dependency versions are immutable; revisions receive distinct version identities.

InformationContent: The abstract informational meaning expressed by artifacts or versions. Content identity requires an explicit equivalence policy and is not inferred from equal strings or file hashes.

VocabularyConcept: A managed terminological information artifact that identifies a vocabulary meaning independently of its labels. It is a vocabulary resource, not automatically a domain universal or the real-world entity denoted.
ClassificationScheme: A governed organization of classification concepts with an identified scope and version policy.

ClassificationTerm: A managed vocabulary item expressing a controlled classification value within an identified scheme. Scheme membership and version context constrain its interpretation. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
ClassificationAssertion: A source-qualified assignment of a classification term to a subject in a specified context.
Tag: A managed annotation artifact carrying a lightweight label. Identical lexical labels do not by themselves identify one tag assignment or imply a formal taxonomy.

RiskRegisterEntry: A managed register record about exactly one RiskCase in this profile. Distinct entries, source systems or registers can record the same case. A software record is an implementation record, not an additional risk subject.
EntryRevision: An identifiable version of a register entry, preserving the content and qualified links effective at its issue.
RiskDescription: A descriptive information item about a risk case, pattern or scenario with an explicit description role and source.
ConsequenceStatement: An information item expressing a possible or reported consequence; it is not the consequence itself.
IdentificationInformation: Recorded information about identifying a risk, including the stated source, channel, agent and available time information.

IntakeChannelTerm: A controlled value naming how risk information entered the registration process; it is not a risk source. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.

DescriptionRoleTerm: A controlled value specifying the function of a description, such as title, summary or scenario description. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.

ConsequenceSlotTerm: A controlled value preserving the source-defined position or role of a consequence statement. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.

RiskRegister: A managed informational register that organizes risk-entry records for a stated organizational scope and purpose. Its documentary identity does not make it an OntoUML collective or physical aggregate.

AssessmentActivity: An actual activity contributing to risk identification, analysis or evaluation. It may cover only part of a risk assessment; the complete standardized assessment process is outside the current process-modeling scope.
AssessmentInformation: A managed information artifact documenting an assessment and its scope, basis, methods, time context, participants and results. It is distinct from performing that assessment.
AssessmentBasis: A specification of assumptions and control conditions under which an assessment result is interpreted.
DimensionAssessmentResult: A result for one assessment dimension, qualified by its method, scale, basis and relevant temporal context.
AssessmentMethodSpecification: A versioned specification of procedures and rules used to produce and interpret assessment results.
AssessmentScale: A governed scale specification defining permissible values or ordered levels for a specified assessment dimension.
RiskScoreResult: A numeric assessment output produced under a declared scoring method; it is not the risk itself or a universal definition of risk level.

AssessmentScaleLevel: A managed vocabulary resource specifying a permissible value or category on an identified assessment scale version. It denotes a level; it is not a measured value occurrence or a bare lexical label.

AssessmentDimension: A managed vocabulary resource specifying an assessment aspect, such as likelihood or consequence severity. The vocabulary item, the aspect denoted and its measured or judged value remain distinct.

EpistemicStatusTerm: A controlled value indicating the evidential or epistemic character of a result, such as observed, estimated or projected. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
TreatmentDecisionInformation: A recorded decision about treating risk, including the selected option, rationale, responsible authority and relevant basis.

TreatmentStrategyTerm: A controlled value identifying a treatment approach; its selection is represented by a treatment decision. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
PlanSpecification: A versioned specification of intended actions, resources, responsibilities, timing and conditions for a stated purpose.
TreatmentActivity: An actual performance of actions intended to modify or otherwise respond to risk, distinct from the plan describing them.

RiskControl: A contextual measure intended to maintain or modify risk. A policy, device, practice or activity may serve as its bearer. Implementation and observed effectiveness are separate claims; one cross-category stereotype is not asserted.
PlanRoleTerm: A controlled value describing the role of a plan, such as primary response or contingency. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
Agent: An entity capable of performing or being accountable for relevant actions, including persons and organizations within the declared profile.
Person: A human individual who may participate in risk management activities or assignments.
Organization: An organized social entity capable of carrying responsibilities and authorizations in the model's scope.
ActorReference: A source-level identifier or description referring to an actor whose identity may be unresolved.
ResponsibilityAssignmentInformation: A recorded statement about an assignment of responsibility or authority, distinct from the relationship it asserts.
ResponsibilityRelator: A temporally qualified responsibility relationship connecting its participants, responsibility scope and grounding assignment.
ResponsibleAgentRole: A context-dependent role borne by an agent with an assigned responsibility.
AuthorizingAgentRole: A context-dependent role borne by an agent authorized to approve or issue a specified decision or assignment.
ResponsiblePerson: A person bearing a responsible-agent role in a specified assignment context.
ResponsibleOrganization: An organization bearing a responsible-agent role in a specified assignment context.
AuthorizingPerson: A person bearing an authorizing-agent role in a specified context.
AuthorizingOrganization: An organization bearing an authorizing-agent role in a specified context.
ResponsibilityRoleTerm: A controlled value identifying the kind of responsibility or authority assigned. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
AnalysisStateTerm: A controlled value describing progress of analysis under a specified analysis-state scheme. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.

WorkflowStateTerm: A controlled value describing handling or processing status under a specified workflow scheme. This is a managed vocabulary resource with scheme-qualified identity, not a bare string.
RecordStateAssertion: A qualified statement about a record's state, preserving the source and available temporal precision.
WorkflowSchemeVersion: An issued version of a scheme defining workflow values and permitted transitions.

WorkflowAssignment: A temporally bounded situation in which a managed record revision has an assigned workflow state under an identified scheme version; the statement documenting this situation is separate.
EvidenceReference: A qualified reference linking a claim or activity to an evidence item, with its intended evidential role and provenance.
EvidenceItem: An information artifact playing an evidential role for a specified claim or analytical activity. The same artifact may be used as evidence in one context and not another.
ObservationActivity: An activity that observes a stated feature of a subject using a declared procedure and temporal context.
ObservationResult: An information result produced by an observation activity, qualified by subject, time, method and available units.

Indicator: A versioned information specification of an observable or computed indicator, including its intended interpretation. A reported indicator value is an ObservationResult, not the specification.

Threshold: A versioned information specification of a context-qualified decision boundary for an indicator or assessment scale, with a comparator, permissible value interpretation and applicability context.
Signal: An information item indicating a potentially relevant change or condition and potentially prompting review; it does not by itself establish a risk event.
RiskCriteria: A versioned information specification of reference conditions used to judge the significance or acceptability of risk in an identified context.

RiskAppetiteStatement: A managed, versioned statement recording the kinds and extent of risk an organization is prepared to pursue or retain, qualified by source framework, objectives, authority and context.

RiskToleranceStatement: A managed, versioned statement recording an organization's stated risk tolerance under an explicitly identified source vocabulary or framework and context. Permissible deviation and readiness to bear remaining risk are retained as distinct source meanings, not silently merged.

RiskCase: An instituted, identifiable subject of enterprise-risk analysis and tracking. It persists across its descriptions, reassessments, responsibilities and administrative record states under a governed identity policy. It is neither its register entry nor a scenario specification nor an actual occurrence.
ObjectiveReference: A managed information item identifying an objective in its source context, without asserting that the information item is the objective.
UncertaintyStatement: A managed statement of what is uncertain about a risk case, including assumptions and evidential limitations; it does not imply a numerical probability.

RiskEvaluationOutcome: A recorded judgment of risk significance or acceptability based on identified assessment information and criteria versions. It is distinct from a numeric score and from the evaluation activity.
ControlReference: A managed identifier or description of a claimed control whose real-world bearer may remain unresolved.

RiskSourceReference: A managed information artifact identifying or describing a claimed contributor to risk in a declared context. The referenced contributor may be unresolved, hypothetical or heterogeneous. The reference does not establish actual causation or an actual occurrence.
ExternalObject: Imported category of substantial endurants (objects) whose identity is supplied by their external kinds. It is a bearer anchor, not an additional Riskium domain or a risk case.
recordsAbout: Proposed identity contract: each entry in this profile concerns one risk case; one case may have several entries.
hasDescription: Each recorded descriptive content has a register-record bearer; shared content requires separate analysis.
classifies: Each classification assignment concerns one subject; multiple schemes and assignments are permitted in the core.
selectsTerm: A classification assertion depends on a specified category; membership is checked against that category's scheme.
belongsToScheme: A category is local to a scheme; correspondence between schemes is a separate relation.
hasBroaderTerm: The core does not prohibit multiple parents; acyclicity and scheme coherence are vocabulary-governance rules.
identifiedRisk: Under this contract, each identification statement concerns one subject; an independent identification activity may discover several subjects.
hasParticipantReference: The source supports multiple participants; mandatory participation is not evidenced.
assignmentAbout: Assignment information concerns one subject and a specified responsibility role.
hasBearerReference: A complete assignment references one bearer; a missing bearer denotes missing assignment information or a separate draft.
assesses: A core assessment concerns one subject; assessment history and parallel assessments are permitted.
hasBasis: Each assessment set declares one basis so that results remain distinguishable; control definitions may remain unknown.
hasDimensionResult: A dimensional result obtains its identity from the assessment set and dimension.
usesScale: An incomplete result or unknown scale is retained; a complete valid result under the selected method has exactly one scale.
selectsLevel: A result may have an ordinal level or a numeric value; the method profile must specify the applicable representation.
levelOf: Each local level depends on one scale and version.
hasScoreResult: The core supports multiple method outputs; an incomplete or uncomputed score is possible.

derivedFrom: A complete derived score has required inputs whose number depends on the method. A fully reconstructed calculation has known inputs; supplied unverified scores are outside this derived-result type.
decisionAbout: Each decision statement concerns one subject; multiple decisions are permitted in the core.
selectsStrategy: A complete decision has one strategy; a combined choice requires several decisions or a separately analyzed method.
planAbout: A plan may cover several subjects; this generalization is a design proposal.
statementAbout: An outcome statement concerns one subject; the two information roles are independent.
hasStateAssertion: A state assertion belongs to an entry; each assertion declares its scheme and value.
hasTag: A general many-to-many relation is a design proposal; actual counts and vocabulary rules remain open.
mayBeRealizedBy: The scenario-to-occurrence link records correspondence without asserting realization or identity.
producesAssessmentInformation: An activity may have several results and a result may involve several activities; the current document establishes neither population.
declaresIntakeChannel: A vocabulary channel differs from a participating agent.
documentsAssessment: Each recorded assessment information item has at least one information bearer; snapshot provenance must be preserved in any relational projection.
documentsClassification: The record holding a classification assertion differs from its classified subject; retrieving two records about one subject requires separate provenance.
documentsAssignment: A recorded assignment is linked to its entry and version; it must not be confused with an assignment from another record.
declaresAnalysisState: Each state assertion uses one declared scheme; a complete analysis-state assertion has one analysis value.
declaresWorkflowState: A complete treatment-state assertion has one treatment value; the two state relations are governed by an exclusive-or constraint for each assertion.
revisionOf: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
previousRevision: Acyclic predecessor relation; branch revisions are allowed in core, not silently flattened.
analyzedInContext: Context must be governed and may be unknown; no domain target or horizon invented.
scenarioAbout: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
expressesScenario: Optional interpreted content link; causal text alone does not instantiate an actual scenario or causal event.
recordsConsequence: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
descriptionRole: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
sourceSlot: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
natureOf: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
declaresNature: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
natureInContext: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.

assessmentContext: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
usesMethod: Unknown method retained; a computed complete profile requires exactly one versioned method.
epistemicStatus: Absent means unknown, never automatically observed or expected.
dimension: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
permitsScale: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
scoreMethod: Computed scores require explicit method version and matching inputs.
assessmentPerformer: Actual activity cannot be inferred from stored results.
recordsIdentification: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
resolvesToAgent: Resolution assertion requires independent evidence; unresolved unit/user labels remain references.
assignmentRole: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
documentsActualMandate: Assignment information can exist without an actual mandate; instantiate the relator only with supported grounding and at least two distinct participants.
mediatesBearer: Positive existential dependency at both ends for instantiated responsibility roles.
mediatesAuthority: Binary mandate pattern requires a distinct real authorizing party.
mandateAbout: Risk referent is aboutness target, not automatic mediation endpoint.
mandateRole: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.

isSpecifiedByPlan: Text-only plans may exist without a known decision record.
executesPlan: Execution needs independent occurrence evidence; Treated state is insufficient.
treatmentPerformer: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
supportsRecordedArtifact: Reference is provenance, not automatic proof of truth.
refersToOccurrence: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.
refersToAgent: Explicit S3 design support; not an independently evidenced historical requirement.

refersToCondition: A context may reference an established predisposing situation; no causal or actual-world assertion follows from free text.
refersToVulnerability: Grounded susceptibility references are optional; uncertain vulnerability content remains information.
refersToExposure: Exposure references require evidenced participants and time context.
hasEstablishedState: Only evidenced risk situations are linked; handling closure does not establish risk cessation.
initiatedBy: An evidenced initiating occurrence may be referenced; causation is not inferred from temporal order.
describesCase: A description may concern a case, pattern or scenario; C-09 requires at least one aboutness target.
describesPattern: Reusable pattern descriptions do not create managed-case identity.
descriptionContext: Description interpretation may be qualified by an explicit context.
scenarioContext: A scenario specification may be interpreted in several contexts; no occurrence is generated.
referencesObjective: Objectives are referenced as information, not silently redefined as reference artifacts.
uncertaintyContext: An uncertainty statement may name its analytical context.
recordsUncertainty: Assessment assumptions and limits are explicit recorded content.
basedOnEvaluation: A treatment decision may cite an evaluation outcome; the outcome is not a score or activity.
recordsRemainingRiskAssessment: Remaining-risk information uses qualified assessment basis and does not imply observed treatment effectiveness.
recordsControlReference: A recorded control claim need not resolve to an actual implemented control.
recordsObservation: Entries can reference observation results without confusing observation with assessment.
specifiesDimension: Method and dimension compatibility is a profile constraint.
scaleForDimension: A scale specification has one declared dimension in this profile; reuse does not equate scales.
thresholdOnScale: C-08 admits a scale anchor independently of an Indicator.
availableInWorkflowScheme: State values require scheme-version context; transitions are scheme content, not a universal process prescription.
referencesControlBaseline: The assessment basis records which control claims were assumed, excluded or retained.
appetiteContext: An appetite statement requires an identified interpretation context.
toleranceContext: A tolerance statement preserves source framework and meaning in context.
authorizerReference: Recorded authorization evidence is distinct from requiring a new organizational approval process.
observationContext: Observation interpretation may have an explicit analytical context.
hasSourceReference: Cases preserve source claims independently of the external source bearer.
sourceReferenceContext: Explicit interpretation context for a source reference; unresolved contextual content remains recorded.
bearsVulnerability: Every actual intrinsic vulnerability has exactly one object bearer. A general external object need not have a vulnerability. Documentary claims alone do not instantiate the mode.

review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: A scenario, consequence statement, signal, plan or report alone must not create actual occurrences, outcomes, controls or effectiveness assertions.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Issued semantic content and effective dependency versions are immutable. Correction and supersession create lineage-preserving new versions.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Results retain method/scale version, dimension, basis, relevant context and time semantics. A score is not the risk, and estimated likelihood need not be numeric.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Recorded time, reference time and validity intervals are distinct. Workflow closure does not prove risk cessation or successful treatment.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: An asserted ResponsibilityRelator requires at least two distinct mediated individuals. If bearer and authority resolve to one actor and no further grounding exists, retain ResponsibilityAssignmentInformation without asserting the relator.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: ResponsibleAgentRole does not automatically mean Risk Owner. Ownership mapping requires recorded responsibility type, accountability, authority and applicable context.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: At least one of thresholdForIndicator or thresholdOnScale is present. If both are present, their scale/unit interpretation is compatible. Qualitative boundaries use scale semantics rather than invented numeric units.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Every published RiskDescription has at least one case, pattern or scenario target. Multiple valid targets are permitted and require explicit interpretation.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Tolerance statements retain source framework/version, original meaning and context. Permissible deviation is not automatically equivalent to readiness to bear remaining risk.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Vocabulary resources retain scheme-qualified identity. Labels are representations and are not OWL classes by default.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: EvidenceReference states an evidential role such as support, challenge or context. Linking a source does not automatically prove the target claim.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: A selected level belongs to the selected scale version and dimension. Results on incompatible methods/scales are not ranked merely by equal labels or numeric codes.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: RiskSource, Consequence and RiskControl remain catalog notions and optional external boundaries, excluded from native formal-core class assertions. Source, outcome and control content is represented by RiskSourceReference, ConsequenceStatement and ControlReference.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Every asserted intrinsic Vulnerability has exactly one substantial-endurant bearer. A reported hypothesis alone is information, not an actual mode.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Raw source content is retained in staging. Managed records require identity, subject, title and provenance. Analytical readiness additionally requires the pinned context, method, scale, basis, dimension and time required for the selected task.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Multiple classifications, descriptions, actors and evidence assertions are retained with role, context, provenance and time. Scalar export requires an explicit selection rule when several values apply.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Direct comparison requires matching pinned method, scale, dimension, basis and temporal context; a governed explicit transformation may enable a different comparison. Missing data is not zero. Reported scores do not imply a reproducible computation.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: State labels are scheme/version qualified. Transition rules and authority are source-backed content. Missing rule means UNKNOWN; Closed does not imply ceased risk and Treated does not imply effectiveness.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: In the terminology adopted by this profile, Risk Item denotes the managed risk subject modeled as RiskCase. This context-qualified mapping does not equate RiskCase with RiskRegisterEntry, RiskScenarioSpecification, ISO risk or any global Risk Item class.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: A reported RiskScoreResult may have no derivedFrom links. A computed RiskScoreResult requires at least one linked DimensionAssessmentResult, a pinned method and adequate inputs. The score kind must be recorded.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Repeated mandates between the same participants are permitted when grounding assignment, responsibility scope or validity differs. Duplicate representations of the same grounded mandate must resolve to one relator identity; participant equality alone is not an identity key.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Every analyzedInContext link is also a hasContext link for the same RiskCase and RiskContextSpecification. The broader hasContext relation may include non-analysis context.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: For each EntryRevision, revisionOf and inherited versionOf identify the same RiskRegisterEntry. previousRevision is irreflexive and acyclic and, when present, relates revisions of the same entry.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: usesContextVersion targets a version of RiskContextSpecification; usesMethodVersion a version of AssessmentMethodSpecification; usesScaleVersion a version of AssessmentScale; usesCriteriaVersion a version of RiskCriteria. Artifact-level references, when present, agree with versionOf.
review_aspects: adequacy of formal or application disposition

groups.claim: Represent risk content, context and evidence without prescribing a management process.
Keep a case distinct from register entries, scenarios, scores and occurrences.
Separate artifact, issued version and expressed content; preserve issued payloads.
Retain method, scale, dimension, basis, context and time with results.
Distinguish supplied scores from calculations with justified pinned inputs.
